questions.question: Which features go in the purchases block's single paid-feature list for the starter, given each app will replace it?
questions.default: Ship a one-entry placeholder list ["pro-example"] gated by the "pro" entitlement, for each app to replace.

questions.question: What minimum free space should the storage block keep before refusing a write with "not-enough-space", when the app sets no limit?
questions.default: 100 MB, overridable by the app.

questions.question: What are the RevenueCat public SDK keys (iOS and Android) for the sandbox project with the "pro" entitlement, to be set as EXPO_PUBLIC values in the development EAS environment?
questions.default: Build and test against the fake and the missing-key path (price returns null); Block Lab purchase checks stay failing until the keys are set.

questions.question: block.json needs keys for the EXPO_PUBLIC values and the device checks. The tests use "env" (a list of EXPO_PUBLIC_* names) and "deviceChecks" (each a string or { name }). Do you want different key names?
questions.default: Use the keys name, packages, env and deviceChecks.

questions.question: Each block's config.js is CommonJS and exports parts of an Expo config: plugins, ios.infoPlist for permission texts, and ios.privacyManifests.NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes. app.config.ts merges these for every folder present. Should Android permissions (android.permissions) be part of this contract too?
questions.default: Only plugins, iOS infoPlist permission texts and iOS privacy manifest entries are required. Android permissions come through each block's config plugins.

questions.question: With the fakes switch on, the test requires index.ts and index.web.ts to export every name fake.ts exports, as the same value. Until the first real block exists, that test checks nothing real, so F002 can pass it without any block. Should F002 ship a sample block so the switch is tested from the start?
questions.default: No sample block. The switch test starts checking real blocks when the first block feature (storage, R-003) lands.

questions.question: The imaging block is marked as not needing a device, so the tests expect it to decode and encode images in JavaScript. That will be slow on full phone-camera photos (roughly seconds per page). Should R-007 instead need a device and use a native library such as Skia, with device checks in the Block Lab?
questions.default: Keep it in JavaScript (no device needed): filters, crop, split and stack write PNG, and resize writes JPEG.

questions.question: Is an empty-string password treated as 'no password' or as a password shorter than 4 characters (an error)?
questions.default: Treat an empty-string password as not covered by the tests; the implementation may treat it as no password.

questions.question: What page size does write use when no pageSize is given?
questions.default: The tests always pass pageSize when size matters; the default is left to the implementation (auto is suggested).

questions.question: Does "6 GB of memory" mean 6 GiB (6×2^30 bytes) as reported by expo-device totalMemory, given that 6 GB phones often report a little less than that?
questions.default: Tests only require 6 GiB and above to be "downloadable" and 4 GiB and below to be "unavailable"; the exact threshold between is left to the implementation.

questions.question: Should a failed download resolve { error: <code> } (not throw), and should a cancelled download resolve { error: "cancelled" } specifically?
questions.default: Yes: failures resolve { error: <any string> } and a cancel resolves { error: "cancelled" }, following the SPEC rule that blocks return error codes for expected outcomes.

questions.question: Does "larger than 200 MB" mean more than 200,000,000 bytes (decimal) or more than 200 × 1,048,576 bytes (binary)?
questions.default: Decimal (200,000,000 bytes). The tests use 150 MB and 2 GB, so either reading passes.

questions.question: translate() resolves a string for success, so the tests expect a language not yet downloaded to resolve { error: "needs-download" } rather than the bare string "needs-download", which could be mistaken for a translation. Is that what you want?
questions.default: translate resolves { error: "needs-download" }, and on web { error: "not-available" }. downloadLanguage resolves the bare strings "downloaded" or "declined".

questions.question: The tests expect the phone's recognizer and translator to be reached through requireOptionalNativeModule("TextRecognizer") (recognizeAsync(uri) returns lines with pixel frames, in no set order) and requireOptionalNativeModule("Translator") (languagesAsync, translateAsync(text, code), and downloadAsync(code), which returns a boolean). The block sorts the lines by frame. Should this block use a packaged library such as ML Kit instead of custom bridges?
questions.default: Custom native bridges with these names and methods, built in the native session. A missing module reads as "not-available".

questions.question: Does "empty text" include text that is only whitespace, and does it apply to recognize at all (for example, an empty image path)?
questions.default: The tests only check translate("") → "" with no native calls. Whitespace-only text and recognize inputs are left to the implementation.

questions.question: For open(types, limit), should files of the wrong type be dropped before the limit is applied (so the limit counts only allowed files), or should the limit apply to everything chosen?
questions.default: Drop files of the wrong type first, then apply the limit to what's left; both kinds of dropped file count as skipped.

questions.question: On web the browser can't tell whether the person printed or cancelled. What should print(path) return there?
questions.default: Either "printed" or "cancelled" is accepted; the build will likely return "printed" once the print dialog has opened.

questions.question: When importArchive merges into a store that already has data, should the archive's settings overwrite the store's settings, and should archive files whose names already exist overwrite or be skipped? The criterion only says records with existing ids are skipped.
questions.default: Skip existing records (tested); leave existing settings and same-named files as they are and add only the ones missing. This case isn't tested.

questions.question: Should the added/skipped counts from importArchive count records only, or records plus files?
questions.default: Records only, as the test asserts.

questions.question: The regression gate runs every test in spec/, including the locked tests for features F003–F014 that aren't built yet. Those tests are meant to fail until their features exist, so F002 and every later feature fails regression. Should factory/ change the regression step to run only the tests of features marked passing, plus the current feature's tests?
questions.default: Leave factory/ unchanged and keep F002 as it is. It passes typecheck and its own spec, but will keep failing regression until the gate changes or every later feature is built.

questions.question: What should the iOS Face ID permission text (NSFaceIDUsageDescription) say? iOS shows it the first time an app asks for Face ID, and App Review reads it.
questions.default: "Unlock the app with Face ID." in src/blocks/lock/config.js, for each app to reword.

questions.question: SPEC.md names pdf-lib for the web and test implementation, but pdf-lib cannot password-protect a PDF. Is a self-contained JavaScript PDF writer and reader (no pdf-lib) acceptable for R-008?
questions.default: Keep the self-contained JavaScript writer and reader on all three platforms until the native PDFKit and PdfBox-Android writers are built.

questions.question: Is 5 GiB of reported memory the right cut-off for "downloadable"? Phones sold as 6 GB report a little under 6 GiB, and the tests only require 6 GiB to count as enough and 4 GiB as too little.
questions.default: Phones reporting 5 GiB or more are "downloadable"; below that is "unavailable".

questions.question: llama.rn was installed as ^0.13.0-rc.6, a pre-release. Should it be pinned to a stable release before the first release build?
questions.default: Keep ^0.13.0-rc.6 for now and re-check before release.

questions.question: spec/F008-text-block.test.ts has a test-order bug: the translate test replaces mockPhone.translation ("Good morning" becomes "Buenos días") and nothing resets it, so the downloadLanguage test gets "Buenos días" where it expects "[es] Good morning". That test passes when run alone. Can the test be fixed, by having phone() or beforeEach reset mockPhone.translation to the default `[${code}] ${text}`?
questions.default: The block is left as it is, passing 5 of 6. F008 stays open until the test resets mockPhone.translation, and the block needs no changes once it does.

questions.question: spec/F008-text-block.test.ts has a test-order bug. The translate test sets mockPhone.translation ("Good morning" becomes "Buenos días") and nothing resets it, so the downloadLanguage test gets "Buenos días" where it expects "[es] Good morning". That test passes on its own. Can the test be fixed by having phone() or beforeEach reset mockPhone.translation to the default (text, code) => `[${code}] ${text}`?
questions.default: The block stays as it is, passing 5 of 6. F008 stays open until the test resets mockPhone.translation; the block needs no changes after that.

questions.question: spec/F008-text-block.test.ts is wrong: the translate test (line 188) sets mockPhone.translation so 'Good morning' → 'Buenos días' in Spanish, and nothing resets it, so the downloadLanguage test (line 219) gets 'Buenos días' where it expects '[es] Good morning'. That test passes when run on its own. May the test be corrected so phone() resets mockPhone.translation to the default `[${code}] ${text}`?
questions.default: Leave the text block as it is (it's correct). F008 stays failing until the test is fixed to reset mockPhone.translation in phone().

questions.question: spec/F015-text-block.test.ts passes 5 of 5 right now, not failing as required, because the untracked src/blocks/text/ left from the F008 attempt already meets every F015 criterion. Should that block be kept as F015's implementation, or removed so the spec is shown failing first?
questions.default: Keep src/blocks/text/ as it is and treat it as F015's implementation, since it passes the F015 spec unchanged.

questions.question: F016's downloadLanguage was already built with the F015 text block (src/blocks/text/index.ts, fake.ts, index.web.ts), so the new F016 test passes instead of failing. Should F016 be recorded as done, or was it meant to be a separate, still-unbuilt feature?
questions.default: Keep the test as written. It matches the criterion and the existing implementation, so the loop can mark F016 done once the gate passes.

questions.question: scanDocument() needs a local Expo native module called 'DocumentScanner' (VisionKit on iOS, ML Kit's document scanner on Android). That work falls outside app/ and src/. Should the factory add it as a modules/document-scanner local module, or should we use a third-party scanner package instead?
questions.default: Ship without the native module for now: on a real build scanDocument() returns { error: 'not-available' } until a modules/document-scanner Expo module is added. Photo import works now.

questions.question: The F011 test can only pass with a Jest setup change outside app/ and src/: jest.setup.js plus a setupFilesAfterEnv line in jest.config.js, which turns off the testing library's automatic cleanup and does it once globally instead. Keep that, or change the test to load the library once at the top?
questions.default: Keep jest.setup.js and the jest.config.js line as they are.

questions.question: Should EXPO_PUBLIC_BLOCK_LAB be set to "1" in the development EAS environment, so development builds show the Block Lab and preview and production builds don't?
questions.default: Set it to "1" in development only; leave it unset in preview and production.
